title: Sicario (2015) and protagonists who hate their movie

commenti.body: She doesn’t want “out” of the film. She wants people to do things legally and not compromise the US’s moral position. But every step of the way she finds out that the US does engage in immoral actions to achieve its goals. It’s a story of her becoming sadder but wiser. She loses in the end. Her loss signals that morality lost. And that the immoral war on drugs will continue.

It might be a bit unfair to call her character the "party pooper" but I know what you're driving at. She volunteered for the mission to stop monsters, and though she ends up becoming a monster like Alejandro herself through her complicity, and she resists the whole way through, trying to be the voice for ethics.

I thought it was also really cool how all the themes are tied together in the ending where Kate feels helpless when he's at gunpoint, and then when she actually has the chance to act, she has to choose between letting him go and accepting her complicity, or killing Alejandro and becoming a monster herself. She loses no matter what she does. Really effective writing.

---
I recently saw an interesting analysis on youtube about how Alejandro is really the main character, but you're watching his story through Kate's eyes. Maybe sorta relevant to your post.
